title: 1. Hook: A World Without Helpers
text: Imagine waking up one morning. You want to drink milk, but there is no milkman. You go to school, but there are no teachers. You fall sick, but there are no doctors! How would our world run without these people?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Why so many jobs?
text: Why do you think different people do different kinds of work instead of one person doing everything? Could one person be a farmer, a doctor, a teacher, and a bus driver all at once?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Chain of Work
content.description: Notice how everyone relies on someone else's work. The farmer grows food, the driver transports it, and the shopkeeper sells it to us.

title: 4. Reveal: What is an Occupation?
text: The work a person does regularly to earn money is called an 'occupation' or 'profession'. Since we cannot do everything ourselves, we depend on people with different occupations to help us live comfortably.

content.definition: The work or job a person does regularly to earn money and help the community.

content.tip: Pause here. Ask the students to imagine a day without any helpers and share one thing that would be very difficult to do.

content.mistake: Thinking that household chores (like cooking or cleaning at our own home) are 'occupations'.
content.correction: Work done at home for our own family out of love is not an occupation because it is not done to earn money. However, if a person does the same work in a restaurant or hotel to earn money, it is an occupation.

content.question: Which of the following is considered an occupation?
options: A teacher teaching in a school

title: 6. Reflection: Who helped you today?
text: Think about the people you met today from the time you woke up to the time you reached school. How many different workers helped you indirectly today? Discuss with your friends.

title: 7. Connection: Work and Workplaces
text: Every occupation is often connected to a specific place in our neighborhood. A doctor works in a hospital, a postman works in a post office, and a teacher works in a school. This connects to what we learned about 'Places in our Neighbourhood'.

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Interview Project
content.description: Talk to your parents or a neighbor. Ask them what work they do, where they go to work, and how their work helps others. Write down their answers and share them in class tomorrow!
